title: Data Scaling Laws for Radiology Foundation Models
research_question: How does radiology pretraining data affect downstream transfer?
dataset_size_sweep: Unique pretraining images: 30k, 50k, 100k, 1M, 3.5M; strictly nested. Three subset/encoder repetitions at the three smallest sizes; one at the two largest; downstream fits use three seeds.
methodology: Compare representation learners with frozen downstream features and attention pooling plus a linear readout. Match methods by wall time within each D; time increases across D (.33 to 40.83 hours).
finding: More pretraining data can improve transfer; the design separates representation learning from downstream evaluation.
relation_to_our_work: Useful precedent for nesting and repeats, but our D varies downstream head-training labels, not encoder pretraining data. Attention pooling also differs from our affine head.
caveats: Do not interpret the abstract as constant compute across D. Exact choices are study-specific; not a universal downstream D range.

title: Task-Oriented Communication with Hybrid-Precision Models
research_question: Can hybrid precision reduce computation in task-oriented communication?
dataset_size_sweep: No standalone unique-training-D grid identified in the reviewed experiments. Fixed ImageNet training corpus; architecture, precision, SNR and communication conditions vary.
methodology: Split ResNet models with a binarized front and full-precision back; OFDM/16-QAM experiments.
finding: Joint precision and transmission choices affect task performance and cost.
relation_to_our_work: Communication-system context for future experiments; does not supply a dataset-size sampling recipe.
caveats: Do not read model depth, SNR or evaluation sample counts as D.

title: Agent-Native Task-Oriented Communication with Joint Token Compression Coding and Modulation
research_question: Can joint token compression, coding and modulation support agent tasks?
dataset_size_sweep: No standalone unique-training-D sweep identified. CLEVR/GQA tasks; 10,000 channel samples describe channel generation, not a labeled-data sweep.
methodology: Train the communication module, then adapt the foundation model with LoRA; compare SNR/bandwidth and task performance.
finding: Task-aware token transmission can trade bandwidth against downstream utility.
relation_to_our_work: Context for a later channel stage; different tasks, representation and trainable components.
caveats: Do not call 10,000 channel realizations a D setting for our classifier experiment.

title: Scaling Laws for Data-Efficient Visual Transfer Learning
research_question: How do pretraining data, downstream data and model capacity jointly affect transfer?
dataset_size_sweep: Uniform samples at 5%, 10%, 25%, 33%, 50%, 70%, 100% for pretraining and fine-tuning data; category set held fixed.
methodology: Vary both data axes and architecture (2/4/6/8 attention heads, head width 64); fit transfer-scaling relationships.
finding: Motivates treating upstream and downstream data as separate variables.
relation_to_our_work: Direct support for a broad same-category downstream-size grid; our study isolates one downstream axis with a frozen encoder.
caveats: Strict nesting, repeat counts and a matched compute budget are not established by the reviewed passage. §5.1 uses inconsistent ImageNet-100/1,000-class wording; retain fractions rather than asserting a resolved absolute count.

title: Budgeted Training for Vision Transformer
research_question: How can ViT training be improved under a computation budget?
dataset_size_sweep: Fixed ImageNet-1k corpus; not a unique-image D sweep. Training components, token fractions and stage lengths change.
methodology: Allocate budgets across attention heads, MLPs and tokens; compare budget-specific baselines including fewer epochs.
finding: Useful efficiency study, not evidence that reducing active tokens equals reducing the dataset.
relation_to_our_work: Helps distinguish computation from unique data and motivates honest exposure accounting.
caveats: Its B denotes a training budget and N can denote tokens. Neither should be copied into our encoder-parameter notation.

title: Beyond Transmitting Bits: Context, Semantics, and Task-Oriented Communications
research_question: What should communication optimize when meaning and task utility matter?
dataset_size_sweep: Tutorial covering multiple systems; no single standardized unique-D sweep identified.
methodology: Conceptual synthesis of context, semantics, task objectives and learning-based communication.
finding: Task performance is a meaningful system objective alongside bit-level metrics.
relation_to_our_work: Supports the thesis motivation and later channel questions; not a direct D-sweep protocol.
caveats: Do not cite this broad tutorial as empirical validation of our sampling or fitted exponent.

title: Feature-Foundation Model Evolution for Low-Latency Semantic Communication
research_question: Can feature and foundation models evolve to handle new semantic classes with low latency?
dataset_size_sweep: VOC2012 segmentation with 15 old classes and online new-class images; no standalone fixed-class D grid identified.
methodology: Transfer foundation knowledge during updates; compare SNR 0–20 dB, compression ratios .2–.6 and latency/new-class conditions.
finding: Studies adaptation to changing semantic content under communication constraints.
relation_to_our_work: Useful future-task context, but class novelty differs from varying labels within our fixed task.
caveats: Image proportions describing novel classes are not interchangeable with distinct classifier-training D.

title: How to train your ViT? Data, Augmentation, and Regularization in Vision Transformers
research_question: How do data, augmentation and regularization affect ViT training and transfer?
dataset_size_sweep: ImageNet-1k versus ImageNet-21k corpora, with 300 versus 30/300 epochs; not a fixed-category nested downstream-size grid.
methodology: Compare model sizes and 28 augmentation/regularization settings; fine-tune downstream models; use validation for selection.
finding: Training recipe and data availability interact; larger corpora need an explicit compute comparison.
relation_to_our_work: Checkpoint lineage and validation discipline are relevant; our frozen probe is a different transfer protocol.
caveats: The roughly compute-comparable 1k/21k comparison changes corpus/classes. Full-model parameter counts include different heads; do not substitute them for our head-removed encoder count.

title: Revisiting Neural Scaling Laws in Language and Vision
research_question: Which scaling functions predict performance beyond the observed range?
dataset_size_sweep: Vision experiments use several pretraining corpora (12M, 100M, 200M, 300M); fitting variable includes examples seen before peak performance. Downstream few-shot tasks are fixed per curve.
methodology: Compare multiple fit families; assess predictions on larger x after fitting lower x, including the x≤xmax/2 versus larger-x split.
finding: Interpolation fit quality does not establish extrapolation accuracy.
relation_to_our_work: Supports forward-size validation and alternative-fit diagnostics. Our robust log-total-loss offset fit is an adaptation, not an exact reproduction.
caveats: Do not transfer their exponents or equate examples seen with unique data. Our fitted floor is not independently identified irreducible error.

title: Scaling Vision Transformers
research_question: How do model capacity, data and computation affect large ViT performance?
methodology: Vary architecture and duration; compare performance and compute envelopes, frozen few-shot transfer and full fine-tuning.
finding: Data and model scale must be interpreted together with compute.
relation_to_our_work: Motivates a broad size range and a later N sweep. Its best-achievable envelope differs from our fixed encoder/recipe curve.
caveats: Nesting and subset repetition are not established by the reviewed passage. Some plot axes are examples seen rather than unique images.

title: Tuning Pre-trained Model via Moment Probing
research_question: Can feature-moment probing improve efficient transfer and few-shot classification?
dataset_size_sweep: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 labeled images per ImageNet class: 1k–16k total; three trials averaged.
methodology: Compare linear probing, moment probing and MP+fine-tuning using an ImageNet-21k-pretrained ViT-B/16.
finding: Few-shot classification provides a direct downstream-label-size comparison.
relation_to_our_work: Closest reviewed precedent for class-aware downstream D and repeated trials; our head uses first-order features and a different backbone.
caveats: Strict nesting and complete few-shot training budgets are not established from the main passage. MP+ changes trainable components; no data-scaling exponent is established here.

title: Scaling Pre-training to One Hundred Billion Data for Vision Language Models
research_question: What improves when vision-language pretraining reaches 100 billion unique pairs?
dataset_size_sweep: 1B and 10B random subsets of WebLI-100B, plus 100B. Nesting of 1B inside 10B is not explicit.
methodology: SigLIP ViT-B/L/H; batch 32k, up to 100B example presentations for each corpus: about 100, 10, 1 passes respectively; evaluate multiple tasks.
finding: Benefits depend on task coverage; unique data and repeated exposure are distinct.
relation_to_our_work: Strong precedent for an exposure-matched comparison as a separate future control.
caveats: Pretraining differs from frozen downstream probing. Source contains an unresolved Appendix reference; this review does not certify every implementation detail.

title: Zero-Shot Semantic Communication With Multimodal Foundation Models
research_question: Can pretrained multimodal features support communication for unseen tasks/classes?
dataset_size_sweep: ImageNet categories partitioned into 800 training and 200 unseen categories; not a fixed-class labeled-D sweep.
methodology: Frozen CLIP ViT-L/14@336 with communication modules; sweep SNR and bandwidth conditions.
finding: Foundation representations can support unseen-category communication objectives.
relation_to_our_work: Relevant to the future channel design and task-generalization controls.
caveats: Class-disjoint generalization differs from our same-class data scaling. Their N=768 feature width is not our encoder parameter count.
